title: Protocols for studying bacteriophage interactions with in vitro epithelial cell layers
protocol: Prepare transwells for use.
Seed MDCK-I cells, or an alternative confluent cell line, into the top chamber of the transwell at a density of 5 × 10^4 to 1 × 10^5 cells/mL in a total volume of 500 μL per well.
Place the pipette tip on the side of the well while seeding to avoid touching or damaging the membrane.
Fill the bottom chamber with 1000 μL of media containing 10% FBS.
Incubate the seeded transwells at 37°C and 5% CO2 until cells reach confluency, typically between two to five days depending on the cell line.
Grow cells in the top chamber of the transwell and check for cell layer resistance.
Once the cell layer reaches confluency, wash the cells and incubate in HBSS media.
Add phages to the top chamber.
After incubation with phages, collect top and bottom samples in a 96 well plate.
Control cell confluency by adding EBD dye to the top chamber.
After incubation, collect samples from both chambers in a 96 well plate.
Ensure a homogenous distribution of cells by gently rotating the plate horizontally following an infinity shape (∞).
Avoid circular shapes as this will push the cells to the side or in the middle of the plate.
Visually inspect the cell layer every day to ensure proper cell growth, density, and homogeneity.
Replace cell culture media every other day.
Tilt the transwell plate at a 45° angle.
Gently place a pipette tip on the side of the inner well.
Carefully remove the media above the cell layer without touching the membrane.
Add fresh media to the chamber following the same process.
Do not add media directly into the cells but rather on the wall of the chamber and let it drip slowly onto the cells.
Always leave a few microliters of media in the well.
Return the transwell plate to the incubator and continue growing the cells until the required cell resistance is obtained.
Use the TEER machine following the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Record daily cell resistances measures until cells reach > 1000 Ω × cm² for MDCK-I cells.
Wash the top and bottom chamber of the transwell with 1 ml of 1× DPBS to remove traces of FBS.
Add 500 μl of Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS) + HEPES (pH 7.4) to the top and bottom chambers without touching the cell layer.
Incubate the transwells for two hours at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Prepare a solution of phages in HBSS-MES at pH 6.
Discard media from both chambers without touching the membrane.
Apply 250 μL of HBSS-MES-pH 6 phage solution to the top chamber.
Apply 250 μL HBSS-HEPES at pH 7.4 to the bottom chamber.
Incubate transwell plate for two to four hours at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Collect a minimum of 150 μL of solution from both the top and bottom chambers and store in labeled 96 well plates until analysis.
Serially dilute the samples collected in the 96 well plate using SM Buffer.
Check the integrity of the cell layer (two hours) after assay completion.
Prepare a 5 mL solution of 0.1% (w/v) Evans Blue Dye (EBD) in 1× DPBS.
Add 250 μL of EBD solution to the top chamber without touching the membrane.
Add 250 μL of 1× DPBS to the bottom chamber.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for one hour.
Collect 100 μL of solution from both the top and bottom chambers.
Transfer the collected solutions to a new labeled 96 well plate.
Measure the absorbance at 620 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute EBD from 0.1 μL to 3 μL of 0.1% (w/v) in 100 μL of 1× DPBS in a separate 96 well plate.
Measure the absorbance at 620 nm for each dilution of EBD to plot an absorbance curve.
Discard wells from analysis if the bottom chamber shows an absorbance higher than 0.05 at 620 nm.
Store unused 96 well plates sealed with parafilm at 4°C for up to one month.
Ensure that no dye leaks from the top to the bottom chamber, indicating maintenance of cell layer integrity throughout the experiment.
Exclude samples from analysis if dye leakage is observed in any well.
Store phages and EBD samples at 4°C before analysis.
Apply a multiplication factor to calculate PFU/mL if collected volume is low (∼100 μL).
Serially dilute the samples from the top chamber for plaque assay quantification of PFUs.
Quantify an undiluted sample and serial dilutions for plaques in the bottom chamber.
Plate at a higher dilution if there are too many plaques.
Plate the undiluted sample with correct dilution factor if there are no plaques.
Seed A549 cells onto microscopy-compatible surfaces, preferably glass-bottom coverslips/slides.
Seed cells at a density between 5 × 10^4 to 10^5 cells/well in a total volume of 200 μL/well of F-12K supplemented with 10% FBS media.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for two to three days until the cells reach the desired density.
Use A549 cells or any other adherent cell line.
Include correct controls for microscopy experiments.
Use unstained cells as a control.
Use cells incubated with SYBR Gold-stained, phage-free media as a control.
Ensure cells are from early passages, not above passage 30.
Perform regular screens for mycoplasma infection.
Add SYBR-Gold stain at a final concentration of 1× to 1 mL of phage lysate with a desired titer of 109 phages/mL.
Incubate the solution in darkness at 4°C for a minimum of one hour or overnight (between 8–12 hours).
Transfer the stained phages to the upper reservoir of a 4 mL - 100 kDa Amicon Ultra centrifugal unit.
Spin at 3220 g (∼4000 rpm) for between 30 seconds and two minutes, ensuring not to spin dry.
Discard the solution from the lower chamber after each centrifugation.
Add fresh HBSS (without phenol red) to the upper chamber.
Repeat steps until the stained lysate appears clear to the eye.
Spin times vary depending on initial phage concentration.
Start with short spin times (less than 30 seconds) and slowly increase as needed, without spinning the centrifugation tube filter dry.
Wash phages four times in HBSS media.
Transfer the filtrate to a new microcentrifuge tube containing around 200 μl of solution.
Resuspend up to 1 ml with fresh HBSS.
Check titer via plaque assay after washing.
Store stained phage solution at 4°C for up to two weeks, but use freshly prepared solutions for best results.
Wash cells three times with 500 μL of warm 1× DPBS per well.
Discard the 1× DPBS from each well.
Add 200 μL of warm F-12K media without FBS to each well.
Incubate for two hours at 37°C and 5% CO₂ to serum starve the cells.
Discard the media from wells.
Add 200 μL per well of 1× Cell-Mask diluted in warm F-12K media without FBS.
Add 200 μL per well of 1× Hoechst diluted in warm F-12K media without FBS.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Discard the media from each well.
Wash cells three times with 500 μL of warm 1× DPBS per well.
Add 200 μL per well of warm HBSS to the cells.
Place the slide under the confocal microscope.
Focus on a field of view using the microscope.
Set the laser's parameters to the optimal setup.
Use an inverted Leica SP8 confocal microscope with HC PL APO 63×/1.40 CS2 oil immersion objective and a hybrid detector (HyD) in sequential mode.
Set the HyD system for the phages channel (480 nm channel) with the highest Line Acquisition number.
Prepare the acquisition to capture one image every 60 seconds to 5 minutes, ideally choosing the shortest time possible without bleaching the sample.
Acquire images for up to 4 hours.
Turn off the lasers.
Discard the HBSS from the well using a pipette without touching the wells.
Add 200 μL of SYBR-stained phages solution at 109 phages/mL, pre-warmed to the microscope temperature.
Close the microscope chamber to maintain humidity and temperature stability.
Re-check the focus after adding the phages.
Begin image acquisition.
Wash cells three times with 1× DPBS after live imaging experiment.
Remove DBPS from each well.
Add 50 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) within a chemical hood.
Incubate for 20 minutes on ice or at 4°C.
Carefully wash cells three times with 1× DBS to remove any trace of PFA.
Leave each well in 200 μL of 1× DPBS.
Open the image stack on FIJI software.
Arrange the channels, ensuring the nucleus is blue, the phages are green, and the plasma membrane is magenta (or as desired).
Split the channels and remerge them to fit the chosen colors.
Add a scale bar to the images on top of the overlay.
Add the time stamp by setting the time between each frame as it was set up at the microscope.
Save the movie with 12 frames per second (fps) or as desired.
Test the presence of phages in the ‘filtered lysate’ using the PFU method described in step 6.
Grow cells in a T25 flask with 6 mL of complete media until confluent.
Split confluent cells into 4 identical flasks.
Prepare a phage solution in cell media at a concentration of 107 - 109 phages/mL.
Add the prepared phage solution to the flasks containing cells.
Incubate the samples for the desired time.
Wash the cells with DPBS to remove excess phages.
Add 3 mL of phages or ‘filtered lysate’ at the desired concentrations to each experimental condition flask.
Incubate the cells and phages together for two hours or overnight (between 8–12 h) at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Optional step: For the control flask, add phages only 30 seconds before the start of washing.
Wash the cells at least three times with ice-cold 1× DPBS to remove excess phages.
Remove as much DPBS as possible from cells and add between 150 to 200 μL of ice-cold Lysis Buffer.
Scrap the cells from the flask with a cell scraper.
Collect the cells in a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Pass the cells three times through a 30 G needle using a syringe or use a cell sonicator four times with between 10 to 15 s intervals.
Lysed samples can be processed for downstream whole-cell analysis techniques.
Trypsinize the cells with 1 mL of trypsin at 37°C and 5% CO2 until the cells detach (around 3–5 min for A549 cells).
Collect detached cells in 5 mL of 1× DPBS and spin the cells for 3 min at 453 g (∼1500 rpm).
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of 1× DPBS and repeat centrifugation two more times to remove non-internalized phages or non-adherent phages.
Collect 1 mL of the supernatant after the last centrifugation as a wash control.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of Lysis Buffer and transfer to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the mixture at RT for 20 min.
Pass A549 cells three to five times through a 30 G needle with a 1 mL syringe to ensure complete lysis.
Prepare samples for intracellular phage quantification using ddPCR as described in the subsection below.
Quantify total phage DNA and/or plaque assay as outlined in step 6 of the “before you begin” section.
Place a few microliters of sample on a glass microscope slide with a coverslip to check under a light microscope at 10× objective.
Ensure that only nuclei and cell debris are present, indicating complete lysis of cells.
Continue passing the cells through the syringe until all cells have lysed if necessary.
Add 22 μL of ddPCR mix per reaction to each well of the ddPCR deep well 96-well microplate.
Transfer 20 μL of the ddPCR mix to the middle row of the droplet cartridge.
Add 70 μL of droplet generation oil to the cartridge row labeled ‘oil’.
Close the cartridge with a rubber gasket.
Place the closed cartridge in the droplet generator and check if the lights are green.
Discard the rubber gasket once droplet generation is complete.
Pipette 40 μL of droplets from each well using a 50 μL pipette and Rainin tips.
Transfer the droplets to the far-left column of a 96-well microplate used earlier, ensuring steady and slow pipetting to maintain droplet integrity.
Seal the plate with an aluminum sheet and a plate sealer.
Use a cold heating block for sealing to avoid warming up the samples.
Place the plate in the thermal cycler according to guidelines for T4-gp23 amplification.
Store the PCR plate in the dark at 4°C for a couple of days before analysis with the droplet reader as the droplets are stable at this temperature.
Place the plate in the droplet reader after running the PCR cycles.
Follow QuantaLife software instructions from Bio-rad to analyze the plate.
Discard the plate once the run has finished and save the data.
For each well selected, check the automatic threshold and manually adjust if necessary.
Between the positive (top/blue) or negative (bottom/black) droplets, adjust the threshold as needed.
Calculate initial sample concentration using the excel spreadsheet provided.
Subtract false positive droplets from all samples to account for background noise.
